naver.title: 성남시 '오리역 제4테크노밸리' 개발 밑그림…용적률 최대 800%
naver.description: 지구단위계획 가이드라인 공고…AI 스마트시티 청사진 제시 경기 성남시 분당구 구미동 오리역 일원을 인공지능(AI) 중심의 '제4테크노밸리'로 육성하기 위한 구체적인 개발 청사진이 마련됐다. 성남시는 부지별 용적률을
naver.content: (성남=연합뉴스) 이우성 기자 = 경기 성남시 분당구 구미동 오리역 일원을 인공지능(AI) 중심의 '제4테크노밸리'로 육성하기 위한 구체적인 개발 청사진이 마련됐다. [성남시 제공. 재판매 및 DB 금지] 성남시는 부지별 용적률을 최대 800%까지 완화하고 맞춤형 개발 기준을 제시한 '오리역세권 제4테크노밸리 지구단위계획 변경 가이드라인'을 6일 공고했다. 이번 가이드라인은 국토교통부 승인 절차가 복잡한 도시혁신구역 대신 시가 직권으로 신속히 추진할 수 있는 지구단위계획 방식으로 지난 4월 사업 방향을 선회한 데 따른 후속 조치다. 가이드라인에 따르면 시는 개발 대상지인 구미동 174 일원 약 57만㎡를 소유 구조에 따라 공공 주도와 민관·민간 주도로 나눠 추진한다. 공공 소유인 성남농수산물종합유통센터 부지(7만2천416㎡)와 법원·검찰청 부지(2만7천702㎡)는 '산업복합용지'로 지정해 AI 앵커기업을 집중적으로 유치한다. 주거시설을 배제하고 업무·교육연구시설을 연면적의 70% 이상 확보하도록 하되 기준용적률 700%에 인센티브를 적용해 최대 800%까지 허용한다. 버스차고지(8만2천449㎡)와 한국토지주택공사(LH) 오리사옥(3만8천211㎡) 부지는 산업·업무·주거가 복합된 '자족복합용지'로 재편된다. 버스차고지 일원은 민관합동 도시개발사업을 우선 검토하기로 했다. 이들 부지와 민간 사유지(7만4천396㎡)는 기반시설 확충 등 공공기여를 전제로 용적률이 최대 800%까지 완화된다. 시는 민간의 다양한 개발 제안을 받은 뒤 내년까지 공공 소유 부지의 지구단위계획 변경을 추진하고 우수기업 유치 공모에 나설 방침이다. 이를 통해 오리역세권을 판교테크노밸리와 연계한 성남 남부권의 새로운 첨단산업 거점으로 육성한다는 구상이다. [성남시 제공. 재판매 및 DB 금지] gaonnuri@yna.co.kr
naver.summary_title: 성남시 오리역 일원 제4테크노밸리 지구단위계획 가이드라인 공개
naver.summary: 성남시가 구미동 오리역 일원 약 57만㎡를 AI 중심 '제4테크노밸리'로 조성하기 위한 지구단위계획 변경 가이드라인을 6일 공고했다. 공공 소유지와 민간지를 구분해 공공 소유 부지에는 AI 앵커기업 유치를 위한 산업복합용지를 지정하고 주거를 배제한 업무·교육연구시설을 연면적의 70% 이상 확보토록 하며, 기준용적률 700%에 인센티브를 적용해 최대 800%까지 완화한다. 시는 내년까지 공공 소유 부지의 계획 변경을 추진하고 우수기업 유치 공모를 통해 판교테크노밸리와 연계된 남부권 첨단산업 거점으로 육성할 계획으로, 용적률 완화와 개발 방식 전환은 대규모 산업시설 유치와 공급망 고도화에 유리하게 작용할 전망이다.

naver.title: LG전자, 美 밴더빌트대에 첫 해외 브랜드 체험공간 개관
naver.description: LG전자가 미국 테네시주 밴더빌트대학교 학생회관에 자사 가전 라인업을 체험할 수 있는 전용 공간을 열고 해외 청년층과의 접점 확대에 나섰다. 4일(현지시간) LG전자는 미국 테네시주 내슈빌 소재 밴더빌트대학교 학생회
naver.content: [디지털데일리 김문기기자] LG전자가 미국 테네시주 밴더빌트대학교 학생회관에 자사 가전 라인업을 체험할 수 있는 전용 공간을 열고 해외 청년층과의 접점 확대에 나섰다. 4일(현지시간) LG전자는 미국 테네시주 내슈빌 소재 밴더빌트대학교 학생회관에 112제곱미터(m2) 규모의 브랜드 공간 '라이프스굿 라운지(Life's Good Lounge)'를 개관했다고 밝혔다. 이번 공간은 서울대, 한양대, 부산대, 울산과학기술원(UNIST) 등 국내 대학에서 운영해 온 체험공간 '어나더 캠퍼스'를 해외 대학으로 확장한 첫 사례다. 개관식에는 박용 LG전자 테네시 생산법인장, 정운태 LG화학 LGCTA법인장, 박효석 얼티엄셀즈 담당 등 계열사 및 대학 관계자들이 참석했다. 라운지 내부에는 ▲올레드 에보 G6 ▲스탠바이미2 ▲스타일러 ▲울트라기어 게이밍 모니터 ▲코드제로 무선청소기 ▲인스타뷰 냉장고 ▲광파오븐 ▲퓨리케어 에어로타워 등 주요 제품군을 배치했다. 취업 정보를 지원하는 학내 커리어 센터에도 스타일러를 설치해 면접을 앞둔 학생들이 의류를 관리할 수 있도록 지원한다. 현장에서는 학생 참여형 프로그램이 운영될 예정이다. 공식 e스포츠 연습 구역으로 지정된 게이밍 존에서는 올레드 게이밍 대회를 개최한다. 엑스붐 노래 경연과 연휴 기간 기숙사에 머무는 학생들을 위한 홀리데이 테이블 행사도 진행한다. LG전자는 라운지를 인재 채용 연계 창구로도 활용한다. 직무 소개와 인턴십 안내, 경영진 및 엔지니어 강연을 마련하고 학부·대학원 연구 과제와 인공지능(AI)·공학 협력을 타진한다. 아울러 테네시 생산법인 견학과 인근에 위치한 LG에너지솔루션, LG화학 등 그룹 계열사와 연계한 산학 교류를 추진한다는 방침이다. 곽도영 LG전자 북미지역대표 부사장은 "라이프스굿 라운지가 활기찬 대학 커뮤니티와의 새로운 접점이 되기를 기대한다"며 "밴더빌트대 학생들이 일상의 긍정적인 경험을 통해 '라이프스굿'이라는 가치에 도달할 수 있도록 지속적으로 지원할 것"이라고 말했다.

semianalysis.title: The Iron(wood) Throne: Google's TPU Stakes Its Claim on Inference
semianalysis.description: Viable Alternative of CUDA Moat, NVIDIA scared and working nights & weekends, Jensen’s Counter Submission, Kimi K3, Muse Spark Open, Qwen, GLM5.3, TorchTPU, vLLM, SGLang, llm-d, Ray
semianalysis.content: In November 2025, we published a newsletter saying that Google is selling TPUs to external customers. Since then, we have been proven right over and over again with Oracle, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta all becoming customers of TPUs just as our Accelerator Model reported. Hardware demand is only half the story, as NVIDIA’s moat has historically been its software and large developer ecosystem. This is where TPU is also making headway, partnering with upstream maintainers across the entire ecosystem, including the Meta PyTorch team, vLLM (Inferact, RedHat), SGLang (RadixArk), llm-d, Ray, etc. This is not a surprise to folks that have read our September 2026 article laying out Google TPU’s externalization strategy. Back in our September article, we published the first third-party TPUv7 results on InferenceX on single-turn workloads, showing that in an apples-to-apples FP8 comparison on Qwen 3.5 397B, TPUv7 Ironwood) delivered up to 50% better performance per dollar than B200 and B300. We also reported that many Google TPU customers were asking for AgentX results, since long-context, multi-turn agentic serving is where inference spend is heading. Previously, Jensen went on the Dwarkesh Podcast and commented on the fact that no other chips were taking advantage of their opportunity to show performance on InferenceX. Six months later, and indeed Google is taking full advantage of this opportunity. Today we are releasing the first official long-context, multi-turn, realistic agentic inference benchmark results on TPUv7 across four models, showing that TPUv7 is either competitive on perf per dollar for external customers or delivers the best state-of-the-art result: Muse Spark Open SGLang AgentX (NVFP4 weights): Competitive TPU performance per dollar result even though the architecture was co-designed for GPUs. Submitted by OSS ecosystem developer, RadixArk (Makers of SGLang). GLM-5.2 vLLM AgentX (FP8): TPUv7 is the cheapest FP8 option, delivering 1.2x to 2.7x the tokens per dollar of B200, B300, and MI355X from 60 to 300 tok/s/user. NVIDIA NVFP4 still beats TPUv7 FP8, but with accuracy / quality loss. Qwen3.5 vLLM AgentX (FP8): With llm-d disaggregated serving, TPUv7 beats GB300 FP8 at every interactivity level and restores parity even against GB300 FP4 at higher quality / accuracy. Kimi K3 vLLM AgentX (MXFP4 weights): Competitive with GB300 NVL72 at launch; With TPUv7 delivering 1.15x to 2.5x the tokens per dollar of GB200, B200, B300, and MI355X. Submitted by vLLM OSS ecosystem developer, Inferact. This was benchmarked on InferenceX/AgentX, the industry-standard inference benchmark supported by almost every major buyer of compute, from Microsoft Azure to Oracle to Meta and many more. Furthermore, it has the support of the ML community, including vLLM, LMCache, SGLang, PyTorch, and Huggingface, and the support of major labs like OpenAI, MiniMax, ZAI, Qwen, Moonshot Kimi, etc. Google potential TPU customers and current TPU customers are asking Google for AgentX results because of how realistic the AgentX benchmark is and how similar it is to their real inference workload. For our SemiAnalysis supply chain shipment estimates on TPUv8i, TPUv8t, TPUv9, TPUv10, check our Accelerator Model for full quarter by quarter breakdown of shipments. Star the InferenceX GitHub repository if you find the open-source benchmark and data useful!. InferenceX is the only inference benchmark in the world to have TPUv7, OpenAI Jalapeño, Nvidia Rubin NVL72, AMD, and soon, SambaNova and Trainium2/3. Recommendation to Jensen NVIDIA only occasionally loses to AMD on some model/scenarios, but TPUs delivering better performance per dollar or competitive performance per dollar is a new experience that NVIDIA senior leadership is unwilling to accept. As soon as TPU posted its first AgentX result on Qwen3.5 397B FP8 showing that even TPUv7 FP8 could beat GB300 NVL72 FP4, NVIDIA tasked a strike force of human engineers and agent swarms to work 997, late into the night until 2am local time and on weekends, across USA and mainland China. Unfortunately for NVIDIA, their first GB300 FP4 counter submission is still 1.64x worse per dollar than TPUv7 FP8 for external customers across most of the curve. We do think that with enough agent swarms, NVIDIA could regain a slight performance lead on GB300 NVL72 FP4 vs TPUv7 FP8, but on NVIDIA FP8 versus TPUv7 FP8, we believe that it is not possible for NVIDIA to regain SOTA for certain models. One thing we hear a lot from open-source maintainers in PyTorch and NVIDIA customers is that there is a lot of bureaucracy; simple things, like adding a new feature to the NVIDIA driver to support a certain feature for PyTorch CudaGraph capture, have been stuck in “internal NVIDIA legal review” for three months. It makes little sense for lawyers to be the blocker for technical driver features. We have seen similar challenges when trying to get NVIDIA to add features like improving ConnectX, NVSwitch, HGX Board (Vulcan, Umbriel) DCGM power telemetry, where it takes a while just to get the timeline for the timeline. In comparison, startup mindset companies like AMD (under the leadership of Anush, Ramine, Vamsi, Lisa) can rapidly develop these features. There needs to be an cultural shift in massively reducing bureaucracy at NVIDIA. This is one of the biggest risks to NVIDIA Moat that Jensen has to tackle. In our experience and many customers experience, Nvidia is now slower moving than AMD, Google, and Amazon to external suggestion, git commits, and feedback. That being said, certain teams at NVIDIA are cutting through the bureaucracy, such as the NVIDIA ex-CentML vLLM team. AMD and TPUs added innovative Megakernel decode support to open source popular production inference engine. Within a week, they were able to defend the NVIDIA by rapidly adding and merging Megakernel support too (PR approved by AMD vLLM maintainer). TPU is making big headway into the ecosystem, and multiple models, like Day 0 Meta’s Muse Spark Open support and Kimi K3.1 Pro already has day 0 TPU support, as it applies the NVIDIA playbook of giving open-source maintainers lots of chips. In contrast, NVIDIA’s contribution of clusters to community maintainers has increasingly been wrapped in DMV style bureaucracy and stingy at best. For a $5 trillion company, one would expect NVIDIA to be more liberal in contributing resources to OSS developers who work for free on improving the NVIDIA stack. We hope Jensen figures out how to eliminate the bureaucracy slowing progress. In comparison, AMD has been increasingly less stingy and providing the upstream vLLM, TileRT, SGLang, Tokenspeed, etc. maintainers liberal access to clusters and rapdily increasing the CI fleet without miminal levels of bureaucracy. Meta’s Muse Spark Open FP4 816B on SGLang TorchTPU Agentic Inference Performance Meta is one of the early adopters of TPU and is already deploying TPUv7 in production using SGLang-TorchTPU. Muse Spark Open is Meta’s latest 816B-parameter open model, and it is one of the launch models for SGLang-TorchTPU. On InferenceX’s agentic inference workload, a submission from RadixArk, a community developer and a lead maintainer of SGLang, shows that TPUv7 is competitive for decode performance per dollar even when using the cost basis of what Meta would pay when buying TPUs. For production inference, Meta uses SGLang for LLM inference and uses vLLM for RL training rollouts. When looking at end-to-end latency, TPUv7 still needs improvements to be competitive, such as continuing to optimize its prefill kernels. For decode kernels, TPUv7 SGLang is using a fully fused megakernel, which eliminates kernel launch latency. Furthermore, the submission uses SGLang HiCache CPU DRAM offloading using Google’s open-source, TPU native TPU-Sync library at high concurrency in order to improve prefix cache hit rates. Note that Muse Spark Open is an extremely GPU-optimized model, and, in theory, not friendly to TPUs at all. This is due to Muse Spark Open’s 64 head dim, which means that for long-context attention, 25% of the systolic array is padded. In comparison, GPU matrix cores consume small tiles, so a wide range of head dimensions, expert widths, and post-sharding KV head counts all land near peak. A dimension of 64 instead of 128 pays close to nothing on an H100 or a B200 and gets a cheaper attention layer for it. GPU architecture allowed researchers to prioritize evaluation performance without a loss in inference performance. This is quite interesting as TPUs can get quite competitive performance on a model that is extremely unfriendly to TPUs. Note that AI labs with lots of TPU capacity, such as Anthropic and Google Deepmind and soon OpenAI, typically co-design their models such that the attention shapes would fit nicely on TPUs to avoid this issue. When TPUs see model architecture with attention head_dim=256, they go full lambo mode. Great work to the RadixArk team on this amazing achievement! They are actively working on updating the documentation such that everyone can get access to this optimized SGLang Muse Spark Open TPU configuration. We expect more AgentX results from RadixArk soon, showing that its SGLang-TorchTPU stack is production-ready. GLM5.2 / 5.3 vLLM AgentX FP8 Agentic Inference Performance GLM-5.2/5.3 is a frontier open model. It is an MoE transformer with 744B parameters and roughly 39B active per token. The model supports a 1M-token context through DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA): a lightweight indexer scores prior tokens, and full attention runs over only the 2,048 selected tokens for each query. For FP8, TPUv7 is the cheapest way to serve GLM-5.2 AgentX. From 60 to 300 tok/s/user, it delivers 1.2x to 2.7x the tokens per dollar of B200, B300, and MI355X at FP8, and 4.4x that of H200 at 150 tok/s/user. FP4 GPUs Still Lead on Perf per Dollar Because GLM-5.3 was not natively QAT with block scale FP4, FP4 has a slight accuracy drop compared to FP8. FP4 GPUs still deliver more tokens per dollar at most speeds, as TPUv7 has no native FP4 support, and we will need to wait until Q1 2027 for TPUv8 with FP4 support, as tracked in our Accelerator & HBM Model. At 100 tok/s/user, GB300 and GB200 FP4 deliver 3.6x and 3.5x the tokens per dollar of TPUv7. FP4 halves the bytes per weight, and small batch decode is memory bound. The SemiAnalysis AI Cloud & TCO Model provides a comprehensive breakdown of pricing across all accelerators currently on InferenceX, as well as many more, including future SKUs such as Nvidia Rubin Ultra and Feynman, AMD MI400 through MI700, Google TPU v8 through v12, and AWS Trainium3 through Trainium6. GLM-5.3 Optimizations GLM-5.3 AgentX contexts reach 1M tokens with over 90% of each request already cached, so KV cache capacity sets how many users fit. There are four main changes: GLM-5.3’s attention reads one shared compressed KV entry per token, so splitting attention heads across devices would copy the whole cache to every device. Decode context parallelism (DCP) splits it by sequence position instead and merges partial attention results every layer. Each query reads only the 2,048 cache entries an indexer selects. TPUv7’s SparseCores, built for scattered memory access, pick those entries and gather them while the TensorCore runs the attention math. TPUv7 uses registers that are 8 rows by 128 lanes. Data must be packed into them, which can fragment. The 128 indexer key bytes plus the scale byte add up to 129, one byte more than a 128-wide row, so the old layout rounded it up to 256. The new layout turns it sideways: tokens now run along each row, and each token’s key runs down 32 four-byte rows, plus one more row for the scale. That comes to 132 bytes, and only 3 of them are wasted. One fused kernel runs routing; the experts, the all-reduce, and the attention merge become a single collective. semianalysis.summary_title: 구글 TPUv7, 장기·다중턴 에이전트 추론서 경쟁력 입증
semianalysis.summary: 구글은 외부 고객용 TPU 판매와 함께 TPUv7(코드명 Ironwood)이 장기 컨텍스트·다중턴(agentic) 추론 벤치마크(AgentX/ InferenceX)에서 여러 모델에 대해 외부 고객 기준 성능당 비용(토큰/달러)에서 경쟁력 또는 최상위를 기록했다고 발표했다. 벤치마크는 Muse Spark, GLM-5.2/5.3, Qwen 3.5, Kimi K3 등 복수 모델을 대상으로 하며, TPUv7은 FP8에서 B200·B300·MI355X 대비 1.2~2.7배, 일부 경우에는 GB300 NVL72 FP4와도 동등 내지 우수한 결과를 보였고(단 FP4는 GPU가 여전히 우위), InferenceX는 주요 클라우드·연구소가 채택하는 업계 표준이다. 이는 TPU가 소프트웨어·생태계 파트너십(예: PyTorch/ vLLM/ SGLang 등)으로 엔비디아의 소프트웨어 우위를 잠식하고 있음을 시사하며, TPU·AMD·GPU 간 성능·비용 경쟁이 추론 인프라·공급망 선택과 클라우드 비용 구조에 직접적인 영향을 미칠 전망이다.
